ai.description: The Bronze Mabuya reaches 7–8 cm snout-vent length. It is olive-brown with dark brown lateral stripes and scattered black spots. It features a smooth, iridescent body and a wedge-shaped snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Bronze Mabuya is best distinguished by its lack of a distinct light dorsolateral stripe, which is typically present in other similar Indian skinks like *E. carinata*.
ai.habitat: The Bronze Mabuya inhabits diverse environments, ranging from dry deciduous forests and scrublands to moist grasslands, typically at elevations from sea level up to 1,500m.
ai.behavior: The Bronze Mabuya is a diurnal lizard that actively hunts insects among leaf litter, often basking on rocks or logs to thermoregulate before retreating to crevices if alarmed.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis macularia* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–8 eggs. Breeding in India typically occurs between March and September, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Bronze Mabuya (*Eutropis macularia*) is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level to 1,500 meters in diverse forest and scrub habitats.
